rationale: Every declaration form Perl accepts for a base class, one per package, because the pre-review rule read only two of the five. `use parent -norequire, 'Base'` (2) and `use base 'Other::Base'` (5) were read, and the option token must not become a parent. `use Mojo::Base -base` (8) passes only FLAGS and the class being subclassed is Mojo::Base ITSELF: the pre-review rule skipped every option-bearing form, so 53 of mojo's 118 inheritance sites produced no edge at all -- the highest-volume defect the F5 differential found. `use Mojo::Base 'Mojo::Base'` (11) names the parent outright. `our @ISA = ('Alpha', 'Beta')` (14) is the pre-Moo form and must give TWO edges. Lines 16-17 are the self-reference case: a class naming ITSELF is a real self-reference in the source and a useless edge in a graph, so it is suppressed. The guard compares FULLY QUALIFIED names, because a leaf comparison also fires for `package Foo::Bar` inheriting a different `Other::Bar` -- and that leaf guard deleted 7 legitimate override edges across mojo and plack, which is what the differential named. Every extends edge carries a line and every overrides edge carries none: the first is written in the source, the second is guessed from a first-parent chain, and `line_number: null` is the harness's way of saying exactly that. UPDATED 2026-10-01: the two `line_number: null` pins on the overrides edges were the UNKNOWN sentinel and are replaced with the real line of the overriding sub. A guessed edge still says so through `confidence: 0.5` and `meta.evidenceClass: inferred` — the confidence is where the guess lives, and the line is a fact about the source. Pinning `null` asserted that the line was unknowable when it is written in the file.
